title: Windsurf vs Cursor
summary: Windsurf vs Cursor: existing Windsurf users reviewing product continuity and an editor alternative.

sections.heading: Resolve identity before features
paragraphs: The official Devin Desktop FAQ says a standard Windsurf update preserves the existing plan, pricing, editor and settings. Compare current public plan prices for a new purchase, but verify the specific account's entitlement, usage and checkout before estimating spend.

sections.heading: Compare only confirmed entitlements
paragraphs: After the account transition is understood, compare one repository change and the controls you actually receive. Until then, a numeric winner would hide the largest uncertainty in this decision.

sections.heading: When neither is a fit
paragraphs: If your required security, data location or operating environment is not supported by current evidence, pause the purchase. Use the sources below to resolve the missing constraint before accepting a recommendation.

verdict: Compare current public base prices and workflow evidence, not historical Windsurf quotes; the vendor documents plan continuity, while each account's actual usage and entitlement still need confirmation.
bestFor: Existing Windsurf users reviewing product continuity and an editor alternative
notFor: New buyers expecting a current Windsurf price from historical research
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Confirm the account's applicable Cognition or Exafunction agreement, Service Tier, any executed DPA or Order Form, training opt-out and enabled persistent features before comparing privacy or retention with Cursor.

pros.text: The vendor identifies Devin Desktop as the new name for Windsurf and says the full IDE remains available after the standard update.
Cursor documents an editor and coding-agent workflow with its own MCP setup and approval controls.

cons.text: The product page describes a standard Windsurf-to-Devin Desktop transition, but this review has not tested an individual account or its entitlement.
Public plan prices are not a workload estimate: confirm current account terms and model usage for both tools before comparing actual spend.

faqs.question: Is Devin Desktop the new name for Windsurf?
faqs.answer: Yes. The current official FAQ says Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf and that the standard over-the-air update preserves plans, pricing, extensions, settings and in-progress work, including legacy Enterprise pricing.

faqs.question: Does that establish the exact monthly cost of a Windsurf-to-Cursor switch?
faqs.answer: No. The vendor describes account continuity, not a shared price basis. Confirm the current plan and usage terms for each account before comparing.

faqs.question: What public Devin Desktop prices can be used in a current comparison?
faqs.answer: The current plan page lists Free at USD 0/month, Pro at USD 20/month, Max at USD 200/month and Teams at USD 80/month plus USD 40/month per full developer seat. Paid usage refreshes daily and weekly and extra usage is at API pricing; these are base amounts, not a total workload or legacy-account quote.

faqs.question: How do Cognition's training terms apply to Windsurf and Devin Desktop?
faqs.answer: Cognition's Privacy Policy says User Content may be used for training depending on applicable terms. Its June 2026 Platform Terms permit Customer Data training and let paid tiers opt out; Teams requires an administrator, and opting out enables provider Zero Data Retention subject to safety, abuse and legal exceptions. The July 2026 DPA sets separate processing and subprocessor limits for applicable personal Customer Data. Windsurf's MSA says its no-training and output-deletion rules are specific to Exafunction Services, with listed exceptions. Confirm the account's controlling agreement, plan, setting and enabled persistent features; none was inspected here.
